presentation: A 59-year-old man with end-stage renal disease who underwent a deceased-donor kidney transplant a few years ago has a remote history of an unprovoked, isolated subsegmental pulmonary embolism in the right lower lobe, now 3.5 years ago. He completed roughly three months of apixaban at that time, without hematology follow-up or additional surveillance, and has remained off anticoagulation with no new clotting events. His routine labs, including serial complete blood counts, metabolic panels, and a recent ferritin of 1059 ng/mL, are stable. He has no ongoing signs or family history of venous thromboembolism or active malignancy on age-appropriate screening. Should the patient resume indefinite anticoagulation given the unprovoked pulmonary embolism?
